verses.text: The revelation the prophet Habakkuk saw:
LORD, how long must I call for help before you hear? I cry, “Violence!” but you don’t save us.
Why do you make me see evil and look at misery? Destruction and violence are right in front of me. There’s fighting, and conflict keeps breaking out.
So the law is powerless, and justice never wins. The wicked close in on the righteous, twisting what is fair.
“Look among the nations and watch. Be amazed—yes, stunned! I am doing something in your days that you wouldn’t believe even if someone told you.
“Look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that fierce, impatient nation. They sweep across the whole earth, taking homes that don’t belong to them.
“They are terrifying and feared. They decide for themselves what is right and honorable.
“Their horses are faster than leopards and fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their riders charge forward; they come from far away, swooping like an eagle rushing to eat.
“All of them come bent on violence. They advance straight ahead and gather prisoners like sand.
“They mock kings and laugh at rulers. They laugh at every fortress, pile up dirt against its walls, and capture it.
“Then they sweep past like the wind and move on. They are guilty; their own strength is their god.”
LORD, my God, my Holy One, haven’t you existed forever? We will not die. LORD, you appointed them to bring judgment; Rock, you established them to punish.

Your eyes are too pure to look approvingly at evil; you cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do you put up with traitors? Why stay silent while the wicked swallow up people more righteous than themselves?
You make people like fish in the sea, like crawling things with no one to rule over them.
The enemy pulls them all up with a hook, catches them in a net, and gathers them in a dragnet. Then he celebrates and is glad.
That’s why he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet: they make his life comfortable and his food rich.
Will he keep emptying his net and killing nations without mercy forever?
